data_notes: No persistence changes. This feature is scoped entirely to web/ (React SPA) and consumes the backend's existing write endpoints (POST /leaves, POST /leaves/:id/submit|approve|reject|cancel). All persistent entities (leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs, notifications, employees, leave_types, leave_policies) already exist and are owned by the backend (src/); their conceptual schemas and repositories are already specified in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and are NOT modified by this feature. The web app has no database of its own — its "persistence" is the bearer token in token-storage (client-side, not a table) and the API client transport layer. No new tables, no new repository interfaces, no new concrete implementations, and no migrations are required. The only new web-side abstractions are the IApiClient write methods (createLeave, submitLeave, approveLeave, rejectLeave, cancelLeave) and the ILeaveService write methods, which are transport/service-layer additions — not persistence. Dates cross the wire as ISO strings (never Date objects) per the existing request<T>() pattern.
transaction_contract: None. This feature performs no multi-step writes in the web layer and owns no database. Each write action is a single HTTP call to an existing backend endpoint; atomicity (status change + balance update + audit + notification) is already owned by the backend's IUnitOfWork/PgUnitOfWork contract, which is out of scope for this web/ change. The web client issues one request per action and reflects the returned status; it does not open or coordinate any transaction.
